t: Under the Marine Insurance Act 1963, at what point must the assured have an insurable interest in the subject matter insured?
o: At the time the policy is effected
At the time of paying the premium
At the time of the loss, though not necessarily when the insurance is effected
At the time of lodging the claim
e: Section 8 of the Marine Insurance Act 1963 provides that the assured must be interested in the subject matter at the time of the loss, though he need not be interested when the insurance is effected.

t: A person who acts as an insurance agent without a valid appointment is liable under Section 42(8) of the Insurance Act 1938 to a penalty which may extend to:
e: Section 42(8) provides that any person acting as an insurance agent without appointment is liable to a penalty up to Rs 10,000, while an insurer appointing such a person may be fined up to Rs 1 crore.

t: As of 2024, the rate of GST applicable on general insurance premiums and on the service component of life insurance premiums is:
e: Insurance services attract GST at 18% (position as of 2024); for life endowment policies GST applies to 25% of the first-year premium and 12.5% of renewal premiums, while pure risk term premiums are taxed in full.

t: Under the IRDAI (Micro Insurance) Regulations 2015, the maximum sum assured for a life micro-insurance product is:
e: The Micro Insurance Regulations 2015 raised the maximum sum assured under life micro-insurance products from Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh; general micro-insurance covers also carry a Rs 2 lakh ceiling.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Advertisements and Disclosure) Regulations 2021, responsibility for the content of advertisements issued by an insurer's agents and intermediaries about its products lies with:
o: The insurer, which must ensure the advertisement is approved as per its board-approved advertisement policy
The Advertising Standards Council of India
e: The 2021 Advertisement Regulations make the insurer responsible for all advertisements relating to its products, require a board-approved advertisement policy and compliance officer approval, and prohibit misleading or unfair advertisements.

t: Under Section 5 of the IRDA Act 1999, the Chairperson of IRDAI holds office for a term of:
o: Five years or until age 65, whichever is earlier
Five years or until age 62, whichever is earlier
Six years with no age limit
e: Section 5 provides a five-year term for the Chairperson subject to a maximum age of 65 years; whole-time members hold office for five years or till age 62.

topic: IRDAI Appointment of Insurance Agents Regulations
t: Under the IRDAI (Appointment of Insurance Agents) Regulations 2016, an individual agent may act for at most:
o: Three life insurers and three general insurers
One life insurer, one general insurer, one health insurer and one each of the mono-line insurers
Any number of insurers provided separate appointment letters are obtained
e: Regulation 3 permits an individual agent to be appointed by one life, one general, one health insurer and one each of the mono-line insurers (e.g. Agriculture Insurance Company, ECGC), with a PAN-based check in the Central Agency Database.

t: A life policy was issued in March 2019, lapsed and was revived in June 2021. The life assured died in August 2025. The insurer discovers that a serious illness was not disclosed in the proposal. Can the insurer repudiate the claim?
o: Yes, because non-disclosure of material facts is always a ground for repudiation
No, because more than three years have elapsed from the date of revival and Section 45 bars any challenge
Yes, provided the insurer refunds the premiums paid
No, unless the insurer obtains IRDAI's permission
e: Under Section 45(1), the three-year period runs from the date of revival (June 2021) and expired in June 2024, so the policy cannot be called in question on any ground, including non-disclosure.

t: Under Section 64UM of the Insurance Act 1938 read with IRDAI's 2020 amendment to the Surveyors Regulations, a general insurer must obtain a report from a licensed surveyor before settling a claim where the loss exceeds:
o: Rs 20,000 for motor and Rs 50,000 for other claims
Rs 50,000 for motor and Rs 1,00,000 for other than motor claims
Rs 1,00,000 for motor and Rs 2,00,000 for other than motor claims
e: Section 64UM(2) read with the IRDAI (Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors) (Amendment) Regulations 2020 fixes the mandatory survey threshold at Rs 50,000 for motor and Rs 1 lakh for other claims (position as of 2024).

t: Under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (as amended in 2019), the fixed compensation payable on a no-fault basis for death and grievous hurt respectively in a motor accident is:
e: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019 substituted Section 164 to provide Rs 5 lakh for death and Rs 2.5 lakh for grievous hurt without proof of fault; claims are adjudicated by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal under Section 165.

topic: IRDAI Surveyors and Loss Assessors Regulations 2015
t: Under the code of conduct for surveyors, a licensed surveyor must decline to survey a loss where:
o: The claim amount is above Rs 1 crore
The insured is a government department
The surveyor has a direct or indirect interest in the insured, the insurer or the subject matter of the claim
The loss occurred outside his home state
e: The Surveyors Regulations 2015 code of conduct requires surveyors to act independently and to disclose and refrain from any assignment where a conflict of interest exists.

topic: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024 - Claims
t: Under the 2024 PPHI Regulations, a life insurer must settle a death claim that does not require investigation within:
o: 15 days of receipt of all relevant documents
30 days of receipt of all relevant documents
45 days of receipt of all relevant documents
e: The 2024 PPHI Regulations require settlement of death claims within 15 days where no investigation is warranted, and within 45 days where investigation is required.

topic: Insurance Act 1938 - Sec 64VB Premium in Advance
t: Which provision of the Insurance Act 1938 lays down that no risk shall be assumed by an insurer unless the premium is received in advance or guaranteed to be paid in the prescribed manner?
e: Section 64VB mandates receipt of premium in advance before assumption of risk, with relaxations under Rules 58 and 59 of the Insurance Rules 1939.

t: A significant change brought about by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015 relating to health insurance was:
o: Health insurance was merged with life insurance business
Health insurance premiums were exempted from service tax
Health insurance business was recognised as a separate class of insurance business under Section 2(6C)
e: The 2015 amendment inserted Section 2(6C) defining 'health insurance business' as a distinct class, enabling stand-alone health insurers with a Rs 100 crore minimum capital.

t: As per IRDAI's Master Circular on Health Insurance Products dated 29 May 2024, the maximum waiting period that an insurer may impose for pre-existing diseases (PED) is:
e: The 2024 master circular reduced the maximum PED waiting period from 48 months to 36 months of continuous coverage (position as of 2024).

t: The payment of an annual fee by every insurer to IRDAI for continuance of its registration is governed by:
o: Section 3A of the Insurance Act read with the Registration Regulations
e: Section 3A of the Insurance Act 1938 requires insurers to pay an annual fee to the Authority, the quantum and timing of which are prescribed in the IRDAI Registration Regulations.

t: Under Section 2(2) of the Insurance Act 1938, the term 'policyholder' includes which of the following?
o: Only the person who originally took out the policy
Any beneficiary named in the policy
A person to whom the whole of the interest of the policyholder in the policy is assigned once and absolutely
The nominee registered with the insurer
e: Section 2(2) defines 'policy-holder' to include a person to whom the whole of the interest of the policy-holder in the policy is assigned once and absolutely, but not an assignee thereof whose interest is defeasible or in whom the interest has vested only for a time.

topic: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations - Interest on Delay
t: Where an insurer delays settlement of a claim beyond the stipulated period, it must pay interest to the claimant at a rate of:
o: Bank rate plus 2%, from the date the claim ought to have been settled
e: The IRDAI PPHI Regulations (2017 and 2024) require payment of interest at 2% above the RBI bank rate prevailing at the beginning of the financial year in which the claim is reviewed.

t: The Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR), with which insurers must upload KYC records of policyholders, is managed by:
o: CERSAI (Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India)
e: CERSAI was authorised under the PML Rules in 2016 to act as the Central KYC Records Registry, and IRDAI mandated insurers to upload KYC records to CKYCR.

t: Under the IRDAI (Outsourcing of Activities by Indian Insurers) Regulations 2017, which of the following activities is an insurer prohibited from outsourcing?
o: Printing and dispatch of policy documents
Core functions such as investment, underwriting, product design, actuarial functions, claim decisions and compliance with AML/KYC
e: Regulation 4 of the Outsourcing Regulations 2017 lists core activities including investment management, underwriting, product design, actuarial, policyholder grievance redressal decisions, claims decisions and compliance that cannot be outsourced.

t: The percentage of obligatory cession to the Indian reinsurer (GIC Re) notified by IRDAI for each general insurance policy for FY 2024-25 is:
e: IRDAI's notification under Section 101A fixed obligatory cession to GIC Re at 4% of sum insured for FY 2024-25 (reduced from 5% earlier), excluding terrorism and nuclear pool business (position as of 2024).

t: In the IRDAI registration process for a new Indian insurance company, Form IRDAI/R1 is the:
o: Application for grant of certificate of registration
e: The IRDAI (Registration of Indian Insurance Companies) Regulations provide a three-stage process: R1 (requisition for application), R2 (application for registration) and R3 (grant of certificate).

t: Following the 2022 amendment to the IRDAI (Registration of Corporate Agents) Regulations, a corporate agent may enter into arrangements with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business (life, general, health)?
e: The IRDAI (Registration of Corporate Agents) (Amendment) Regulations 2022 raised the limit from 3 to 9 insurers in each of life, general and health (position as of 2024).

t: All government grants, fees and charges received by IRDAI are credited to a fund called the:
o: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Fund constituted under Section 16
e: Section 16 of the IRDA Act 1999 constitutes the 'Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Fund' to which all grants, fees and sums received by the Authority are credited.

t: Under IRDAI's Point of Sales Person guidelines, a POSP is permitted to solicit and market:
o: Any insurance product of the sponsoring insurer
Only pre-underwritten, simple products approved by IRDAI for POS channel, such as motor, travel, PA, home and simple term/endowment products
e: The POS guidelines (2015 for general/health, 2016 for life) restrict POSPs to simple, pre-underwritten products where the policy is largely system-generated with no underwriting discretion.

t: Which of the following is a TPA NOT permitted to do under the TPA Regulations 2016?
o: Provide cashless facility through network hospitals
Reject or repudiate a health insurance claim in its own name; the decision rests solely with the insurer
Maintain a 24x7 call centre for policyholders
e: TPAs provide health services like pre-authorisation and claims processing, but the final decision to admit or repudiate a claim can be taken only by the insurer, not by the TPA.

t: Which of the following was newly introduced by the Consumer Protection Act 2019 compared to the 1986 Act?
o: Establishment of the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) and provision for mediation and e-filing of complaints
e: The 2019 Act created the CCPA to regulate unfair trade practices and misleading advertisements, introduced mediation cells and e-filing, and allowed filing where the complainant resides.

t: The Insurance Advisory Committee constituted under Section 25 of the IRDA Act 1999 may consist of not more than how many members, excluding ex-officio members?
e: Section 25 provides that the Insurance Advisory Committee shall consist of not more than twenty-five members excluding ex-officio members, representing commerce, industry, transport, agriculture, consumer fora, etc.

t: 'Bima Bharosa' is:
o: IRDAI's deposit insurance scheme for policyholders
A micro-insurance product for rural women
IRDAI's online integrated grievance management portal, which replaced the earlier IGMS, for registering and tracking complaints against insurers
e: Bima Bharosa (launched 2022) is IRDAI's rebranded Integrated Grievance Management System that allows policyholders to lodge complaints online and track their status with insurers.

t: A certificate of registration granted to a corporate agent by IRDAI is valid for a period of:
e: Under the IRDAI Corporate Agents Regulations 2015, the registration is valid for three years from the date of issue and is renewable thereafter.

t: What is the minimum paid-up equity capital prescribed under Section 6 of the Insurance Act 1938 for an Indian insurance company carrying on life, general or health insurance business?
e: Section 6(1) prescribes a minimum paid-up equity capital of Rs 100 crore for life, general and health insurers; the amount was retained in the 2015 amendment.

t: Under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017 (as amended in 2021), the maximum value of a complaint (including expenses) that an Insurance Ombudsman can entertain is:
e: Rule 17(1) of the Insurance Ombudsman Rules 2017 as amended in 2021 caps the award (including expenses) at Rs 50 lakh, raised from the earlier Rs 30 lakh (position as of 2024).

t: The legal recognition of electronic records and electronic/digital signatures, which underpins e-insurance policies and e-proposal forms in India, flows from:
o: Sections 4 and 5 of the Information Technology Act 2000
Section 10 of the Indian Contract Act 1872
e: Sections 4 and 5 of the IT Act 2000 give legal recognition to electronic records and electronic signatures, enabling IRDAI's framework for e-insurance accounts and electronic issuance of policies.

t: The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015 raised the permissible foreign investment in an Indian insurance company from 26% to:
e: The 2015 amendment to Section 2(7A) of the Insurance Act raised the composite foreign investment cap from 26% to 49%, subject to the company being Indian owned and controlled.

t: An award passed by the Insurance Ombudsman is:
o: Binding on both the insurer and the complainant
Advisory in nature for the insurer
Binding on the insurer, which must comply within 30 days of receipt of the award and intimate compliance to the Ombudsman
Appealable by the insurer to IRDAI
e: Rule 17(6)-(8) of the Ombudsman Rules 2017 makes the award binding on the insurer, which must comply within 30 days; the complainant may still approach other forums if dissatisfied.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations 2018, the minimum capital/net worth requirements for direct, reinsurance and composite brokers respectively are:
o: Rs 50 lakh, Rs 2 crore, Rs 2.5 crore
Rs 75 lakh, Rs 4 crore, Rs 5 crore
Rs 1 crore, Rs 5 crore, Rs 10 crore
Rs 25 lakh, Rs 1 crore, Rs 2 crore
e: Regulation 22 of the Brokers Regulations 2018 prescribes minimum capital of Rs 75 lakh for a direct broker, Rs 4 crore for a reinsurance broker and Rs 5 crore for a composite broker.

t: Which section of the Insurance Act 1938 requires every insurer to obtain a certificate of registration from the IRDAI before commencing insurance business in India?
e: Section 3 of the Insurance Act 1938 prohibits any person from carrying on insurance business in India without a certificate of registration issued by the Authority.

t: A certificate of registration issued to an insurance broker under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations 2018 is valid for:
o: Perpetual validity subject to annual fee
e: Regulation 14 of the Brokers Regulations 2018 provides that the certificate of registration is valid for three years, with renewal applications to be made at least 30 days before expiry.

t: IRDAI requires every insurer to maintain a 'control level of solvency' expressed as a solvency ratio of at least:
e: Under Section 64VA and the IRDAI (Assets, Liabilities and Solvency Margin) Regulations 2016, insurers must maintain a solvency ratio (available to required solvency margin) of 150%.

t: Under the PML Rules and IRDAI's AML/CFT guidelines, a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) must be filed with FIU-IND within:
o: 7 working days of arriving at a conclusion that the transaction is suspicious
15 days of the end of the month
e: Rule 8 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules requires the Principal Officer to furnish STRs within seven working days of being satisfied that the transaction is suspicious.

topic: IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024 - Grievances
t: As per the IRDAI Protection of Policyholders' Interests Regulations 2024, an insurer must resolve a policyholder's grievance within:
e: The 2024 PPHI Regulations require insurers to resolve grievances within 14 days of receipt, replacing the earlier 15-day norm, and to acknowledge them immediately.

t: Under the amended Section 39 of the Insurance Act 1938, a nominee who is the parent, spouse or child of the policyholder is treated as a:
o: Beneficial nominee entitled to the policy proceeds
e: Section 39(7), inserted by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015, makes parents, spouse and children beneficial nominees who are beneficially entitled to the amount payable, not merely receivers on behalf of legal heirs.

t: An agent offers to pass on half of his first-year commission to a prospect as an inducement. What is the maximum penalty prescribed under Section 41 of the Insurance Act 1938 (as amended in 2015) for such rebating?
e: Section 41(2), as substituted by the Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act 2015, prescribes a penalty extending to Rs 10 lakh for offering or accepting a rebate of premium or commission.

t: The Public Liability Insurance Act 1991 requires compulsory insurance to be taken by:
o: Every owner handling hazardous substances, to provide immediate relief to persons affected by an accident, with contribution to the Environment Relief Fund
Every owner of a motor vehicle
Every company listed on a stock exchange
e: Section 4 of the PLI Act 1991, enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy, mandates owners handling hazardous substances to insure against liability to give no-fault relief under Section 3 and contribute an equal amount to the Environment Relief Fund.

t: The 2024 Health Insurance master circular requires insurers to decide on cashless pre-authorisation requests and final discharge authorisation within:
e: The master circular mandates decision on cashless authorisation within 1 hour of request and final discharge authorisation within 3 hours of receipt of the hospital's discharge request.

t: Under the IRDAI (Re-insurance) Regulations 2018, every Indian insurer must file its board-approved reinsurance programme for the forthcoming year with IRDAI:
o: Within 30 days after the start of the financial year
At least 45 days before the commencement of the financial year
e: Regulation 3 requires insurers to submit the board-approved reinsurance programme at least 45 days before the start of the financial year, with final treaty slips within 30 days of commencement.

t: Under IRDAI health insurance regulations, an insurer may deny renewal of an individual health insurance policy only on grounds of:
o: Adverse claims experience of the policyholder
The policyholder attaining 65 years of age
Change in the insurer's product portfolio
Fraud, moral hazard or misrepresentation or non-cooperation by the insured
e: Health policies are required to be renewable lifelong and renewal cannot be denied except on grounds of fraud, misrepresentation, moral hazard or non-cooperation by the insured.

t: A key change introduced by the IRDAI Commission/EoM Regulations 2023 is that:
o: Product-wise commission caps were removed and insurers may pay commission as per a board-approved policy, subject to the overall EoM limit
Commission was abolished for all life insurance products
Agents' commission was capped at 10% for all products
Commission is now payable only by cheque
e: The IRDAI (Payment of Commission) Regulations 2023 did away with segment-wise commission caps, giving insurers flexibility within the overall expenses of management ceiling.

t: The statutory obligations of insurers towards the rural and social sectors are contained in which sections of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: Section 32B (rural or social sector) and Section 32C (obligations in respect of rural and social sectors) empower IRDAI to prescribe minimum percentages of business in these sectors.

t: The Life Insurance Council and the General Insurance Council are constituted under which provision of the Insurance Act 1938?
e: Section 64C of the Insurance Act 1938 constitutes the Life Insurance Council and the General Insurance Council as bodies of all insurers, each functioning through an Executive Committee under Sections 64F and 64G.
